# Using delulu-smash

## How to answer (for the AI)

- Lead with the answer in a line, then the steps for what was asked. Not the whole section.
- Show examples as the guide does: what to type, then what the user will see.
- **End with one thing to paste, when there is one**: a code block holding exactly one command, ready to
  run as it is. Real values, not placeholders (`/vods mkleo vs sparg0`, not `/vods <text>`), using the
  user's own variables and names from the chat when they fit. No comment or second line in that block:
  its copy button copies everything in it.
- Leave that block out when nothing can be pasted (a key press, a click, a "the guide doesn't cover it").

## The window

Five panels. Each has an `Alt` key that shows or hides it; add `Shift` for full screen (again to go back).

| Panel | Key | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Chat | `Alt+A` | ask the AI, type slash commands |
| Results | `Alt+R` | what tools returned, one tab each (`r1`, `r2`, ...) |
| Python | `Alt+J` | Jupyter-style cells; the same names are Python objects |
| Variables | `Alt+V` | every name you have, with type and size; clear them here |
| Terminal | ``Alt+` `` or `Alt+Enter` | a shell on this machine (experiment). `Alt+I` in it: ask AI for a command; it is typed at your prompt, not run |

- Only the chat shows at first. The bottom bar has a toggle per panel; `/results`, `/python`, `/variables`
  and `/terminal` do the same from the chat.
- Each panel's top right has ⤢ (full screen) and × (hide). Hiding keeps what is in it.
- With every panel hidden the window shows your desktop wallpaper; the panel keys are first in `Alt+H`.
- `/config` opens the app's settings (today: `background`, that picture). Empty = default; Run applies it.
- `Alt+F` floats the result you are in over the page, or fills the window with your panel. Esc puts it back.

## Chat

- Enter sends, Shift+Enter is a new line. ArrowUp in the empty box brings back earlier messages.
- Each tool result is a row, eg `r1 · tool · 10 VODs`: click it to unfold it there, `open →` makes it a tab.
- Under an answer: what it cost, eg `$0.0011 · 21.3k in · 812 out · 3 requests`.
- The title bar shows how full the conversation is (`context 4%`) and the spend: this session and this month.
  Yellow past half full: `/clear-chat` starts a new, small conversation.
- `/clear-chat` can't be undone. It drops the chat and what the AI remembers; variables and spend stay.

## Slash commands

Type `/` in the chat box: a list opens. Type to filter, Tab completes, Enter runs, Esc closes.

- A message starting with `/` runs in the app and is never sent to the AI. You type them; the AI can't.
- A known command is blue as you type, an unknown one orange.
- A command that takes no text does nothing when text follows it (`/clear-chat please` clears nothing).
- Show or hide: `/results`, `/python`, `/variables`, `/terminal`, `/help`, `/keys`, `/debug`.
- Others: `/new-cell` (a Python cell), `/close-tabs` (every Results tab; the variables stay).
- The full list is at the end of this guide.

## Widgets

A widget is a view you add: `/vods`, `/usage`, `/smashdb`, `/browser`. It shows in the chat under the command;
`open →` makes it a tab. The `+` in Results and the palette add one as a tab.

```
/vods mkleo vs sparg0 grand finals     the AI fills the form, you press Run
/usage tweek offline, last 60 sets     same, for a player's characters and results
/smashdb                               a SQL console over the frame-data tables
/browser                               a web page in a frame
```

- **The AI only fills the inputs; you run them.** Change any input first, or type a new instruction to refine.
- In a result that has inputs, `Alt+I` (or the robot button by `Inputs`) opens the same Ask AI row.
- SmashDb console: tables on the left, query on the right, Ctrl+Enter runs (a selection runs alone).
- A link clicked in an answer opens in the Browser as a glance over the app; Esc closes it. Sites that
  refuse to be framed (GitHub, start.gg) open in a real browser tab.

## Variables and @

Every result has a name: `r1`, `r2` from the AI's tools, `q1` from a SmashDb console, `out3` from a cell,
plus whatever your cells assign. `@name` in the chat points the AI at one.

```
@q1                                    prints it, no AI
@q1 who has the best win rate?         ask about it
@q1.char which of these beat Steve?    one column (or @r3.df, @r3.sql)
@big.describe() anything odd?          one read-only method call, at the end
@big.sql("select * from self where wins > 3")
how do @r1 and @r2 differ?             several at once
```

- Typing `@` lists the variables; `.` after a name lists its columns and the methods allowed.
- A small table is sent whole; a big one as its shape, columns and first 5 rows.
- Only one call, last, with plain values: `@q1.filter(pl.col("wins") > 3)` and `@q1.head(5).tail(1)` are
  refused, and the message is put back in the box. Use `.sql("...")`.
- **Clearing**: the × on a row in Variables, tick rows then `Clear`, or `/clear-variables` for all. An
  `Undo` button shows for 3 seconds; after that the memory is really freed.

## /assign: a variable the AI writes

```
/assign top5 = the five best players in @q1     you name it
/assign the date Ultimate came out              the AI names it
/assign aapl = daily closes for the past year from https://www.google.com/finance/quote/AAPL:NASDAQ
```

- A box shows the code. Edit it if you like; Enter runs it, Esc drops it, Shift+Enter is a new line.
- The line under the code says where the value comes from: your data, the AI's knowledge (not checked), or
  a web page (read by AI when run, not checked).
- It can hold text, numbers, dates, lists of those, or records. A DataFrame is refused, with why.
- A web page takes a few seconds; one that needs a browser 30 to 60 s and a few cents.

## /script: keep a browser run as a script

After an `/assign ... from <url>` that needed the browser, its row ends with "/script saves it as a script".

```
/script              save the last such run (or /script prices to name it)
/script list         what is saved
/script delete <id>  delete one
```

- The draft is run with no AI and must give the same rows. It then shows as code in the box: Enter saves,
  Esc drops.
- From then on `/assign` proposes `name = scripts.<id>(...)` when one fits: about 5 s and free.
- When a script stops working the browser gets the value instead, the row says why, and `/script` proposes
  the repaired file.

## Python cells

`pl` (polars) and `db` (SmashDb) are there already; `r1`, `q1`, ... are real objects (tables are DataFrames).

- Shift+Enter runs and moves on, Ctrl+Enter runs in place, Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs all.
- `Alt+N` new cell below, `Alt+Backspace` delete this one, `Alt+↑` / `Alt+↓` move between cells,
  `Alt+Z` clears every output.
- Tab completes from the live variables (`r1.` lists real methods).
- `Alt+I` in a cell: say what you want, the AI's change shows as a diff. Tab accepts, Esc discards.
- A cell ending in a table shows it; "Open as tab" keeps it as `out<n>`.

## Results

- Click a tab to switch; × or right-click closes (Close Others, Close All, Show in Chat).
- A table: type in the filter box, click a header to sort. The grid shows at most 2000 rows.
- `SQL ▸` in a table's bar: a query box on that table (it is `self`), Ctrl+Enter runs, × goes back.
- VODs: click a card to play it; "Show list" brings the list back.

## Finding things

| Key | Opens |
| --- | --- |
| `Alt+P` | the command palette: every action by name, and `Go to: r1` for open results |
| `Alt+K` | every keyboard shortcut, searchable |
| `Alt+H` | help: examples and fixes |
| `Alt+D` | the debug log: every request made, the agents' setup, spend, memory |

## Fixes

- An answer says a key or token isn't stored, but you stored it: run `ds settings sync` in a terminal (it
  restarts the app).
- The app doesn't answer: `ds ui status`, then `ds ui restart`.
- Variables are kept until the app's server restarts.
